brief: A small-parts organizer with at least six separate bins.

requirements.evidence: 7 joined full cells, each holding a half-depth bin. Shallow trays suit small parts, as the screw, nut and standoff heaps placed in them show.
7 separate bins: six hex-bin-half bins at the outer cells and one hex-bin-half-div3 in the middle. That makes 9 separate compartments.

finish.summary: I built a compact small-parts organizer from 7 hex cells: one in the middle with six around it. Each cell has a half-depth bin, which gives 9 separate compartments in total. The middle bin is split into 3 and the six outer bins are open. I closed all open outer faces with end caps and bolted the joints together. To show what it's for, I put screws, nuts, standoffs, solder and tape in the bins. They sit below the bin rims, as loose parts do, but you can see all of them from above. check_build reports no rule issues, no prop warnings, and the mesh collision check is clear. It comes to 32 parts and about 3,033 g of filament.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
